newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close broadly lower, blue-chips down.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close broadly lower, blue-chips down.

text.p: Malaysian equities closed broadly lower on Tuesday in spite of blue chips posting a mild rebound in late trading.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading stocks was down 1.24 points at 1160.85. The all-share EMAS index was down 1.02 to 334.85, and the Second Board index was off 10.85 to 626.25.
"It's been very quiet. Most UK fund managers are on holiday, and regional funds are taking a wait-and-see attitude," said Tony Shue, institutional dealer at Jupiter Securities.
Total volume was at 316 million shares valued at 2.55 billion ringgit. Losers led gainers 429 to 143.
"It's been a typical post-budget week so far, with nothing new to look forward to, and with investors selling on news," said an institutional dealer at a bank-backed securities brokerage.

YTL closed down 10 cents to 14.40 ringgit. The infrastracture developer announced after the market closed that it was withdrawing its bid to acquire a controlling interest in Hong Kong power utility, CEPA.
"The news is neutral for YTL. Nobody was buying the stock on the expectations" that YTL would make a bid, said Adin Jarjis, power analyst at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
